Reddit has announced two upcoming changes that are likely to upset some long-time users.

The company has already imposed one restriction on Old Reddit, and has now announced a second. Additionally, RSS support is also being discontinued…

Old Reddit

Reddit significantly revamped its user interface back in 2018, which drew strong backlash from users who preferred the original layout. In response, the platform stated it would keep what became known as "Old Reddit" available as long as users continued to use it.

The first shift in this policy came back in August, when the company required Old Reddit users to be logged in. Reddit has now announced that the original interface will only be available to users who have used it within the past six months, and new users will not be able to access it.

Reddit says both measures are aimed at reducing AI scraping of its content (though apparently not when those companies pay).

RSS Feeds Are Being Discontinued

Reddit has announced it will be discontinuing RSS feeds, citing the same reasoning.

This may pose particular problems for Subreddits that rely on RSS to carry out Moderation processes. Reddit says it is aware of this and suggests Moderators use Devvit apps such as Discord Relay.

Users Are Not Happy

From the comments on the post, it's clear many long-time users are very unhappy with these latest developments.

What do you think of these latest changes? Let us know in the comments.
